info.title: romulus
info.description: DBA as a service: versioned Postgres schemas, diffs and collaborative drafts.

get.summary:
The IdP's redirect back: exchanges the code, verifies the ID token,
upserts the user and starts a session. Requires a verified email.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set by the IdP instead of `code` when sign-in did not happen.

get.summary:
Starts signing in: redirects to the IdP's authorization endpoint (code
flow, PKCE S256, state, nonce).

parameters.name: next
parameters.description:
Where to land afterwards: a path under `/app`. Anything else is
ignored (the app's home instead).

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description:
`select_account` asks the IdP which account to use even when one is
already signed in there ("switch account").

parameters.name: login_hint
parameters.description:
The address to sign in with (an invitation's): the IdP pre-fills it,
or offers to create the account. Anything not shaped like an email

cookie. The web app then navigates to `redirect_url` to end the IdP
session too.

one goes on under a new cookie.

Imports migration files as versions, from CI: the API token's database.

parameters.name: format

The signed-in person's acceptance of the Terms, and where the legal

Accepts the Terms in force (the box at sign-in), in the language they

get.summary:
Starts an authorization (OAuth 2.1, 4.1.1): checks it, then sends the
browser to the consent page.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: One the client registered (any port on a loopback one); optional when it registered only one

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Optional (PKCE protects the flow): echoed back unchanged, 1024 characters at most

303.description: Always to the consent page, never to the redirect URI: `/app/oauth/authorize?request=…` (with the cookie that binds the request to this browser); `?refused=…&client_id=…&redirect_uri=…[&state=…]` for a bad request (the page offers the way back); `?error=…` when the client or its redirect URI is unknown

get.summary:
The way back to a client after its request was refused, for the
consent page's "Return to" link. Signed out too: refusals come before
signing in. Answers only for a registered client and one of its
redirect URIs, so the link can lead nowhere else.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The request's own, when it had one.

404.description: Not a refusal romulus makes, an unknown client, or a redirect URI it did not register

post.summary: Registers a client (RFC 7591): any MCP client may, without signing in.

429.description: Too many registrations from this client (`Retry-After`)

get.summary: The authorization request this browser started, for the consent page.

404.description: Expired, answered, or started in another browser

post.summary:
Allows or denies an authorization request: answers where to send the
browser (back to the app).

404.description: Expired, answered, or started in another browser

422.description: A scope wider than the app asked for

post.summary:
Revokes a token (RFC 7009): a refresh token ends its whole grant, an
access token itself. Answers 200 whatever the token was, so it tells
nothing about tokens it did not revoke.
Exchanges a code, or a refresh token, for tokens.

get.summary: The organizations the caller belongs to, by name.

post.summary: Creates an organization; the caller becomes its admin.

403.description: `single_org`: this install keeps one organization; `terms_required`: the Terms of Service are not accepted yet

get.summary: One organization the caller belongs to.

404.description: No such organization, or not a member

patch.summary:
Renames an organization, moves it to another slug, or changes how many
approvals publishing needs. Admins only.

402.description: `plan_limit`: more approvals than the plan allows (hosted billing)

get.summary:
The organization's plan, subscription and usage against every cap. Any
member reads it; admins change it.

404.description: Billing is off on this server, or not a member

post.summary:
Starts paying for a plan: as a business or a consumer (never assumed),
the Terms accepted, a business's statement and name, or a consumer's two
requests (recorded with the session, 10 years, and in the audit log),
then a Stripe Checkout Session to send the browser to. Admins only, in
person. An organization already subscribed changes plan in the portal.

409.description: `already_subscribed`: change plans in the portal; `checkout_completed`: another checkout was just paid; `checkout_copy_changed`: the boxes' wording changed, reload

422.description: `validation` naming the field: no buyer chosen, the Terms or a box not ticked, a business's name or country missing, or Free

get.summary: The organization's invoices, newest first. Admins only.

post.summary:
A Customer Portal session: payment method, invoices, plan changes
(upgrades now, prorated; downgrades at the period's end) and
cancelling, straight on the cancel page with `{"flow": {"type":
"cancel"}}`. Admins only.

409.description: `no_customer`: never subscribed; `no_subscription`: nothing to cancel or change

post.summary:
Withdraws from the organization's plan (a consumer, within 14 days of
subscribing): recorded and acknowledged by email at once, the
organization on Free, the subscription cancelled and the days not used
refunded through Stripe. Admins only, in person (not with an access
token).

403.description: `not_a_consumer`: a business's plan is cancelled instead; `not_for_agents`

503.description: `billing_unavailable`: Stripe could not be read; `withdrawal_by_email`: a payment romulus cannot refund itself (withdraw by email). Nothing was recorded

get.summary: The organization's databases, most recently active first.

404.description: No such organization, or not a member

post.summary: Creates a database (with no version yet). Developers and admins.

402.description: `plan_limit`: the plan's databases are all used (hosted billing)

422.description: `validation`, `details` names the field; `major_unavailable`: this server has no sandbox for that Postgres major

get.summary: One database.

404.description: No such database (or organization)

delete.summary:
Deletes a database: it disappears from the organization, its versions
are kept but unreachable, its API tokens stop working, and its slug can be
used again. Developers and admins.

patch.summary:
Renames a database, moves it to another slug, or changes its
description. Developers and admins.

get.summary: The database's audit events, newest first. Developers and admins.

post.summary:
Compiles SQL without storing anything: its errors, or what it would
change against the latest version. Developers and admins.

get.summary: Compares two versions: what changed from `from` to `to`, three ways.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The version compared from: the left side, `before` in the diff.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description:
The version compared to: the right side, `after`. May equal `from`
(nothing changed), or be older (the diff then reads backwards).

400.description: `bad_request`: a number that is not one

402.description: `plan_limit`: a version past the plan's history window (hosted billing)

404.description: `not_found`: no such database, or no such version

get.summary:
The open drafts of a database, most recently edited first, with who has
each open.

post.summary:
A new draft from the latest version, ready to edit: no form, renamed
later if wanted. A schema draft by default; with `{"mode": "migration"}`,
a migration from the latest version, written from scratch.

requestBody.description: Optional: a schema draft without one

get.summary: One draft (published ones too: the editor says what became of them).

delete.summary: Deletes an open draft. Whoever has it open is told and let go.

409.description: Published drafts stay with their version

patch.summary: Renames an open draft; everyone in it sees the new name at once.

post.summary: Approves the draft's SQL as the caller reviewed it.

403.description: `edited_draft`: they edited it, someone else approves; `editors_unknown`: a developer or admin, on a draft whose editors are unknown

503.description: The draft could not be loaded

409.description: `draft_published`: its approvals are the version's now

get.summary: The migration publishing the draft now would call for.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
The migration tool: its file names, transactions and down migration.
`plain` when absent.

parameters.name: concurrently
parameters.description:
Build indexes on existing tables `CONCURRENTLY`, outside the
transaction (their own files where the tool needs it).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description:
The description in file names (made file-name safe); by default the
target version's message, or `v4_to_v5`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description:
The first file's version, where the tool numbers its migrations:
Flyway's `V<version>` (digits and dots; by default the target
version's number), or the number other tools put first (digits: a
golang-migrate sequence like `000042`; by default the time,
`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`). Files after it take the next ones.

parameters.name: renames
parameters.description:
Renames turned on or off, over what is stored (the draft's choices,
the versions'): a JSON object of rename keys
(`SchemaMigration.renames[].key`) to `true` or `false`, like
`{"column/public/users/email/email_address":false}`.

parameters.name: sha256
parameters.description:
What the person reviewed (the publish preview's `sha256`, or a live
compile's SHA-256 of the SQL; in migration mode it covers the base
too: `compile::input_hash`): the migration of exactly that, or 409
`draft_changed`. Required: a migration is never of a text unseen.

400.description: `bad_request`: an unknown format, no `sha256`, `renames` that is not a JSON object of booleans

409.description: `draft_published`: its version has the migration now; `draft_changed`: not the text reviewed (`sha256`); `stale_base`: update the draft first

422.description: `compile_failed`: the SQL has errors (`details.diagnostics`); `migration_unreadable`: a migration written by hand that does not parse, or holds a `ROLLBACK` or a savepoint

post.summary: Switches the draft between schema mode and migration mode.

409.description: `draft_changed` (it kept changing: try again), `draft_busy` (being published or updated), `draft_published`

422.description: `compile_failed` (`details.diagnostics`): the SQL has errors, so there is no migration to start from; or the migration does not apply to the current base, so there is no schema to go back to. `unrepresentable` (`details.objects`): no SQL romulus can keep compiles back to the schema the migration made

get.summary: The diff publishing would create, for the confirm dialog.

post.summary: Publishes the draft as the next version.

409.description: `draft_changed` (review again), `renames_changed` (a rename was switched since: review the migration again), `stale_base` (update the draft first), `draft_published`, `draft_busy` (someone else is publishing it), `passing_test_required` (the organization requires a passing migration test of this text)

422.description: `compile_failed`: the SQL does not compile (`details.diagnostics`); `unrepresentable`: in migration mode, no SQL romulus can keep compiles back to the schema (`details.objects`)

429.description: `rate_limited`: the checks publishing compiles (migration mode) count against the compile limits

get.summary:
Up to when the caller read each thread of the draft (threads never
opened are not listed).

put.summary: Marks a thread of the draft read up to `at` (never back).

404.description: No such draft, or no such thread in it

put.summary: Turns renames of the draft's migration on or off.

post.summary: "Request review": the drafts list shows the draft waits for one.

delete.summary: The draft no longer waits for a review.

get.summary: The draft's source and its compile.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Wait (a few seconds at most) for the compile of the text as it is.

put.summary: Writes the draft's source: the whole text, or edits of it.

409.description: `draft_changed` (not the text read: read it again), `draft_mode_changed`, `draft_published`, `draft_busy` (being published or updated)

422.description: `validation`: neither or both of `text` and `edits`; `edit_not_found` / `edit_ambiguous`: an edit's `old` is not in the source, or more than once (`details.edit`, from 0)

post.summary: Rewrites the draft's SQL in canonical form.

409.description: `draft_changed` (it kept changing: try again), `draft_published`, `draft_busy` (being published), `migration_mode` (the draft is edited as a migration)

422.description: `compile_failed` (the SQL has errors, `details.diagnostics`), `tidy_unsafe` (the canonical form would change the schema)

post.summary: Brings the latest version into the draft: see the module documentation.

409.description: `draft_published`, `draft_busy` (being published or updated), `draft_changed` (rewritten meanwhile, try again)

503.description: The draft could not be loaded

Starts an upload of migration files, with some or none. Developers and

422.description: `validation` (a path, a part, too many or too large files), `invalid_file`

get.summary:
An upload: its files, and its import's progress or outcome. Its starter
only.

post.summary:
Adds files to an upload (a path and part sent again replaces it).
Developers and admins, the upload's starter only.

422.description: `validation` (a path, a part, too many or too large files), `invalid_file`

Imports an upload's files: what the import refuses is answered at once,
otherwise it runs on (202); read the upload to follow it. Developers and

anything: what moving the database there would meet. Developers and
admins.

422.description: `validation`: not a supported major; `major_unavailable`: this server has no sandbox for it

The description in file names (made file-name safe); by default the
target version's message, or `v4_to_v5`.

parameters.name: version

parameters.description:

get.summary:
The newest tests of a draft, of a pair of versions, of a version's own
migration, or of the database: without their reports (`summary` says
how each went).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The tests of the migration from `from` to `to`.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description:
The tests of the migration version `version` was written or
imported as.

post.summary:
Tests a migration on a playground of its own, filled with generated
rows: up, checks, down, checks. Answers at once with the test, queued;
`GET` it for its place in line, its progress, then its report.
Developers and admins.

402.description: `plan_limit`: a size or playground hours beyond the plan (hosted billing)

get.summary:
One test: its place in line or progress while it runs, its report once
it ran.

post.summary:
Acknowledges the data loss a test found that the migration does not
declare (`needs_acknowledgement`): the test then counts as passed (an
up-only one as passed up only: never enough for the publish gate), and
the audit log keeps who did, with the test. Developers and admins; where
the organization requires a passing test, not the draft's own author or
editors (someone else looks at the loss), unless an admin.

403.description: `own_draft`: the draft's author or an editor, where the organization requires a passing test (someone else, or an admin)

post.summary:
Stops a test that waits or runs, and deletes its playground. Developers
and admins.

get.summary: The database's live playgrounds (building, ready, failed), newest first.

post.summary:
Creates a playground for a draft (its base version) or a version, and
builds it in the background: `GET` it for the progress. Developers and
admins.

402.description: `plan_limit`: a size or playground hours beyond the plan (hosted billing)

get.summary: One playground, with what its host says now.

delete.summary:
Deletes a playground: its cluster on the host, its history. Developers
and admins.

get.summary:
Opens the playground's console: one Postgres session (read-only) per
socket. Text frames: `ConsoleRequest` in, `ConsoleEvent` and
`ConsoleNotice` out. Close codes: 1011 the host is unavailable, 1012
server restarting, 4001 membership changed (reconnect), 4401 session
ended, 4404 deleted, 4429 too many consoles open.

402.description: `plan_limit`: the organization used its playground hours (hosted billing)

post.summary:
Runs the draft's migration on the playground's rows (reset first). The
answer streams `PlaygroundMigrationEvent`s, one JSON per line (blank
lines keep the connection alive), the last one `done` (the report) or
`failed`. Developers and admins.

200.description: The progress, one event per line

402.description: `plan_limit`: the organization used its playground hours (hosted billing)

409.description: `playground_not_ready`, `playground_expired`, `playground_busy`, `migration_in_progress` (yours, elsewhere), `draft_not_open`, `playground_stale` (the draft moved to another base), `draft_changed`

post.summary: Runs SQL on the playground, read-only, and answers its results.

402.description: `plan_limit`: the organization used its playground hours (hosted billing)

Role.description: A member's role in an organization (`member_role`).

renames.description:
The renames turned on or off as the person sees them, over the
draft's (`SchemaMigration.renames[].key` → on or off).

sha256.description:
What the person reviewed: the draft's live compile SHA-256 (the
migration tab's), so a run is never of a text nobody saw (409
`draft_changed` when the draft moved on).

RunsPage.description: A page of the history, newest first.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

ScheduledChange.description: A change Stripe will make at the end of the period (a downgrade).

SchemaDiff.description:
Everything that differs between two schemas, matched by schema and name:
a rename is a removal plus an addition.

Lists hold only what was added, removed or changed. [`SchemaDiff::status`]
is the total view (every object of either side, unchanged ones included)
for highlighting a graph.

entities.description:
Tables, partitioned tables, views, materialized views and foreign
tables, by schema then name. Partitions are listed under the entity
their chain of parents leads to, not here.

database.description: The database's slug, and its name.

name.description: The table (or view…) the hit is or is in; the enum's name.

type.description: A column's type; an enum's labels, comma-separated.

version.description: The version searched: the database's latest.

SchemaMigration.description: A migration, as statements and as the files of one tool.

archive.description: What the files download as together: `<version>_<name>.zip`.

destructive.description: How many statements delete data or can fail on existing rows.

files.description: The files to put in the tool's migrations folder, in order.

from.description:
The version migrated from; `null` for nothing (a draft of a database
without versions).

pg_major.description: The Postgres major it is written for: the database's.

renames.description:
Every rename considered, known or detected, applied or not: what a
person turns on or off (`renames` in the request, by `key`). For a
migration written by hand, they shape its down migration only.

statements.description: In order; the same whatever the format.

to.description:
The version migrated to (for a draft, the number publishing it would
give).

warnings.description:
What to know before running it (a column that ends up elsewhere, a
possible rename, a type recreated…).

written.description:
The up migration is a draft's, written by hand (migration mode):
`statements` and the files' up migration are its statements as
written, in its order (data statements included; its `BEGIN` and
`COMMIT` left to the tool, the files split where it commits), each
one's hazard (and `destructive`) read from what it does to existing
rows rather than planned; the down migration, where the tool has
one, is still planned from the schemas, in the first part's files.

oneOf.description:
The first event after connecting: how the server treats this
connection.

read_only.description:
Document updates from this connection are dropped (reviewers,
and everyone once the draft is no longer open).

role.description: The connection's role in the organization.

oneOf.description:
The latest compile of the draft's SQL. Sent to everyone after each
compile, and to each connection when it joins.

diagnostics.description:
Errors (when `failed`), then notes. Spans count UTF-16 code
units in `utf16_start`/`utf16_end`, like `Y.Text` in the browser.

model.description:
The model when `ok`. When `failed`, the last model that compiled,
sent only on joining (others already have it); keep showing the
previous one when absent.

schema_sql.description:
In migration mode, with `model`: the schema it is, as SQL
(read-only: the migration is the source). Absent otherwise.

sha256.description:
Hex SHA-256 of the SQL compiled. A client whose text hashes the
same can place `diagnostics` as they are; otherwise a newer
compile is on its way.

oneOf.description:
The draft switched modes (docs/MVP.md "Review round 1", item 2):
the doc's `meta.mode` changed in the same transaction as its texts.

To one connection: its last edit changed the text that is not the
source in `mode` (sent before it saw a switch), and was undone.

The draft's status changed (publishing started, failed or
succeeded; the draft was deleted).
The draft was renamed.

The database has a new version (another draft was published): if
it is not this draft's base, publishing now needs "Update draft".

Someone moved the database to another Postgres major: the draft
compiles on it from now on (a compile follows).

An admin removed a version: if it is this draft's base, publishing
now needs "Update draft" (onto the latest version left).
An admin restored a removed version.

Approvals and the review request (`collab::review`): sent on joining
and whenever they change (an approval, an edit resetting them,
someone becoming an editor, the organization's setting).

approvals.description:
Approvals of the SQL as it is now, by members who did not edit
it, oldest first: these count.

editors.description: Who changed the SQL: they cannot approve it.

editors_unknown.description:
Edited before romulus recorded editors: only reviewers (who never
could edit) may approve it.

outdated.description: Approvals of an earlier text: an edit since reset them.

oneOf.description: The review the editors asked for, if they did.

required.description: Approvals publishing needs (the organization's setting); 0: none.

oneOf.description:
The server could not store some edits (its database failing): they
live in the open tabs only.

To one connection: what became of its comment operation `id`
(`MESSAGE_COMMENT`). When `ok`, the doc's update came first.

The draft was updated to a newer version ("Update draft"): its base
is now `version`; `conflicts` blocks are left to resolve.

ServerEvent.description: A message only the server sends (tag 100 on the websocket), as JSON.

renames.description:
Rename keys (`SchemaMigration.renames[].key`) to `true` (apply it),
`false` (do not), or `null` (romulus's own choice again).

Sides.description:
The same thing on both sides, `null` where it does not exist.

For an object it is the DDL `remus-sql` renders for it alone (statements
separated by blank lines, ending with a newline), so the web can show the
two side by side. For a part of an object it is the one-line definition:
a column's type and clauses, a constraint's `pg_get_constraintdef`, an
index's `CREATE INDEX`, a policy's clauses after `ON table`, a partition's
bound.

org.description: The organization the account joins once created.

SignUpPolicy.description: Who may create a password account (`ROMULUS_SIGNUP`).

redirect_url.description:
Where the browser goes next: the IdP's logout (which comes back to
the sign-in page), or the sign-in page itself.

oneOf.description:
The organization joined, when the sign-up came with an invitation
and finished.

new_account.description:
This report made the account's row (its first, within the hour of
signing up): a sign-up just completed.

SignupSource.description: The source of the visit signing up, as its URL carried it.

referrer.description:
The site that linked here (the homepage's `ref_origin`, or
`document.referrer`); only its origin is kept, and nothing when it
is this site.

SkipReason.description: Why a statement is not replayed.

SkippedStatement.description: A statement not replayed, located in its file.

Span.description:
A range of a SQL text, `start..end`, in bytes, UTF-16 code units and
line/column.

end.description: Byte offset just past the last character.

start.description: Byte offset of the first character.

to.description: Where `end` is (the position just past the range).

utf16_start.description: `start` in UTF-16 code units: a JavaScript string index.

StartCheckout.description:
What the buyer states before paying (Terms 3.4 c, 3.5 and 9.3): as whom,
and the boxes of each, in the words of `checkout_copy_version`.

accept_terms.description: The Terms of Service in force are read and accepted.

business_confirmed.description:
A business: subscribing for its trade, business or profession, on
behalf of the business named, authorised to bind it (the professional
edition's box adds: not as a consumer).

oneOf.description:
Required, never assumed, when consumers may buy (`consumer_sales`):
a business or a consumer. Businesses only otherwise: absent, or
`business`.

company_name.description:
A business: its name and country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), required;
its VAT or registration number, optional.

copy_version.description: The version of the wording the boxes showed.

immediate_start.description:
A consumer expressly asks for the service to start before the
withdrawal period ends…

oneOf.description: The language of the page: the payment page's and the contract's.

withdrawal_acknowledged.description:
…and acknowledges paying for the service until a withdrawal, and
losing the right once it is fully performed.

Status.description:
Where an object, or a part of one, stands between the old and the new
schema.

StatusMap.description:
Status of every object on either side, unchanged ones included.

Schema-qualified objects are nested by schema, then name, both unquoted
exactly as in the model: `status.entities["shop"]["orders"]`. Nesting keeps
keys collision-free without making the web reproduce Postgres's quoting
rules (a flat `schema.name` key cannot tell schema `a.b` + table `c` from
schema `a` + table `b.c`). Extensions are database-wide, keyed by name.

SubscriptionInfo.description: The subscription, as Stripe last said.

amount_cents.description: What a period costs, in cents.

current_period_end.description:
The end of the period paid for: the renewal date (or the end, when
cancelled at the period's end).

grace_until.description: While a payment is overdue: when the plan stops holding.

Summary.description: Counts per category, and the same as one sentence.

counts.description: Categories with at least one change, in [`Category`] order.

text.description: `"3 tables added, 1 changed; 1 enum changed"`, or `"no changes"`.

color.description:
A color name (`stone`, `red`, `amber`, `green`, `teal`, `blue`,
`violet`, `pink`); the web app draws an unknown one as `stone`.

members.description: Qualified names of the tables in it.

TableHistory.description: A table, view, materialized view or foreign table, and its parts.

id.description:
Unique in the timeline: `schema.name` of its last state (a suffix
`#2`… in the rare case two objects end under one name).

schema.description: Its schema and name in its last state.

TermsStatus.description: The signed-in person and the Terms.

accepted.description:
The person accepted the version in force (true when there are no
Terms).

accepted_version.description: The latest version the person accepted, and when; `null`: never.

oneOf.description:
The language of their contract and billing emails; `null`: never
chosen (the app follows the browser).

required.description:
This server has Terms (the hosted service); false on a self-hosted
install, where the rest is empty.

TestData.description: The rows a test runs on.

oneOf.description:
The playground whose rows were copied for the test; `null` for rows
generated for it.

seed.description:
Hex: the same model, size, profile, seed and generator give the same
rows.

TestDraft.description: The draft a test is of.

TestGate.description:
What the publish gate of an organization requiring a passing test
(`organizations.require_passing_test`) says of a draft as it is: the
publish dialog shows it, publishing enforces it ([`gate`]).

available.description:
Tests can run here (playgrounds on this server, the database on
their Postgres major).

nothing_to_test.description: Nothing to test: no base version (no rows yet), or nothing to run.

passing.description:
The newest test of exactly the migration publishing would run that
counts: passed up and down on rows (or its undeclared loss
acknowledged).

reason.description: Why it holds publishing, when it does.

required.description: The organization publishes only migrations that passed a test.

TestPlayground.description: A playground a test ran on a copy of.

TestProgress.description: What a running test is doing.

oneOf.description: Its playground's build, while building.
The statement running (from 0) of `statements`, and which way.
The phase running, while testing.

waiting.description: Why it waits for room, when it does.

TestStage.description: Where a test is, while it is not over.

TestSummary.description: A test's report in a line, for lists.

data_loss.description:
Findings of data that does not come back, and of those, the ones no
flagged statement explains.

TextEdit.description:
One edit: `old`, exactly as it is in the source and found once,
replaced by `new`; or, with `old` empty, `new` appended at the end.

ThreadRead.description: Up to when the caller read a thread.

thread.description: The thread's id in the draft's doc.

changed.description: Whether the SQL changed (false: it was tidy already).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the SQL as Tidy left it.

Timeline.description: A database's history, object by object.

earlier.description:
Versions older than the first one listed, left out (the timeline
holds the newest 1000).

layout.description:
The newest version's positions and groups, then older versions'
positions for tables it does not have (each table where it last
was), and their groups for tables only older versions had.

versions.description: Oldest first: the states' `from` and `to` are indexes in this list.

access_token.description: `rmls_oat_…`, for `Authorization: Bearer` at the MCP endpoint.

refresh_token.description: `rmls_ort_…`, single use: each refresh answers a new one.

TokenScope.description: What an API token may do (`api_token_scope`).

TypeHistory.description: An enum, a domain or a composite type.

TypeKind.description: `pg_type.typtype` of a column's type, as a word.

slug.description: Changing it changes every link to the database (pushes use its id).

require_passing_test.description: Whether publishing a draft needs a passing migration test.

slug.description: Changing it changes every link to the organization.

base_version.description:
The version the draft is based on now (`null`: the database has
none).

changed.description: Whether anything changed (already on the latest version: nothing).

conflicts.description: Conflict blocks in its SQL now: publishing waits until none is left.

diagnostics.description:
Migration mode: the migration's errors on the new base, located in
it (absent when it still applies, and in schema mode).

UploadImportOptions.description:
How to import an upload's files (all optional: a bare `POST` detects
the format and refuses to append).

append.description:
Import even though the database has versions that were not
imported: the imported ones continue the numbering.

dry_run.description:
Replay without storing anything: the files are kept, to import for
real next.

oneOf.description: Read the files as this tool's; detected from them when absent.

message.description: What changed, in a line (at most 1000 characters).

sql.description: The schema as SQL DDL, at most 1 MiB.

UploadedFile.description: A file, or a part of one.

content.description: The file's text (UTF-8), exactly as it is on disk.

part.description:
For a file too large for one request: which part this is, 1, 2…
(joined in order). 1 by default.

path.description:
Its path relative to the repository (or to the migrations folder),
with `/`: `db/migration/V2__add_invoices.sql`,
`prisma/migrations/20240101000000_init/migration.sql`. The import
reads the tool and each migration's name from paths. Never absolute,
never `..`.

Usage.description: Usage against every cap of the plan in force.

approvals.description: The approvals publishing needs, and the most the plan allows.

hidden_versions.description: Versions kept but hidden by the plan, every database together.

history_days.description: Versions older than this are hidden; `null`: all are shown.

schema_size.description: The largest schema (tables and views) among the latest versions.

versions.description: The database with the most versions.

VersionApproval.description: An approval of the draft a version was published from, as it was then.

author_name.description: Their name when they wrote it.

approvals.description:
Who approved the draft it was published from, when the organization
required approvals (`drafts::approvals::freeze`); oldest first.

layout.description:
Table positions and groups, keyed by qualified name (empty until a
draft arranges them).

oneOf.description: The migration file it was imported from (origin `import` only).

model.description: The remus model (`remus_core::Schema` as JSON), canonical.

source.description:
What was uploaded or pushed, verbatim: SQL, remus JSON, or the
migration's up SQL for imports.

written_migration.description:
Published from a draft in migration mode: the migration it was
written as is at `…/versions/{number}/migration`.

diff.description:
From `from`'s model to `to`'s: the change list, the summary and the
status of every object for the graph.

layout.description:
Where the union's tables sit: the newer version's positions and
groups; the older one's positions for tables the newer did not place
(the ones it removed, say), each in its old group if the newer one
still has it, or in its old group alone if not.

models.description: Both models: the graph draws their union, styled by `diff.status`.

sql.description:
Both models as SQL, rendered the same way whatever their source (an
upload's text or a push's JSON): canonical order, and the newer
version's header on both, so a line diff of the two shows only what
the schema changed.

VersionLayout.description: Where tables sit, and their groups.

layout.description: Top-left corner of each table in graph coordinates, by qualified name.

VersionMigration.description: The migration an imported version came from.

id.description: The tool's version of it, or its file name for plain folders.

path.description: The file, relative to the folder imported.

skipped.description:
What was not replayed (`SkippedStatement[]`, lines in the version's
`source`: the migration's own text).

VersionOrigin.description: How a version came to be (`version_origin`).

VersionPage.description: A page of versions, newest first.

hidden.description:
Older versions kept but not listed: past the plan's history window
(hosted billing). They come back with a plan that keeps them; an
export holds them all.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

VersionPostgres.description:
The Postgres a version was compiled on (uploads, drafts, imports: the
sandbox of its database's major) or pushed from (remus JSON: the real
server). Versions keep it when their database moves to another major.

database_major.description: The major its database targeted when it was created.

major.description: `server_version`'s major; `null` when it does not start with one.

other_major.description:
Pushed from a server on another major than its database targeted
then: the history flags it, and offers to move the database.

oneOf.description: `null` once the person's account or the token is gone.

message.description: What changed, in a line; `null` when none was given.

number.description:
1, 2, 3… per database, never given twice (a removed version leaves
its number unused).

written_migration.description:
Published from a draft in migration mode: the migration it was
written as is at `…/versions/{number}/migration`.

VersionTexts.description: A version's model in every format the viewer shows.

sql.description:
The source for SQL versions; rendered from the model for pushed JSON
and imported migrations.

VersionThread.description: A thread of a version's discussion.

created_by.description: Who started it (`null` once their account is gone).

frozen.description:
From the review of the draft the version was published from, as it
was then: read-only.

read_at.description: Up to when the caller read it (`null`: never opened).

oneOf.description: The language of the page, which the acknowledgement is written in.

WithdrawalInfo.description:
The withdrawal right of the subscription, for a consumer's: until when
it can be used, or the withdrawal made. `null` for a business.

last_day.description: The last day it can be used, in Paris.

until.description:
The end of the withdrawal period while it runs (midnight in Paris
after `last_day`).

Withdrawn.description: A withdrawal, as the billing page shows it.

completed.description: Stripe cancelled the subscription and made the refund.

refund_cents.description: What is refunded: the days not used.

WrittenMigration.description:
The migration a version was written as, in a draft in migration mode:
from the version before it (nothing, for a first version) to it.

from.description: The version it migrates from; `null` for a first version.

sql.description: The migration, as written (data statements included).
